title: A Peg Stability Module is a vault in disguise, which is why it needs a debt ceiling
content:
A.3.3.2.1.1 describes the Peg Stability Module as letting users "swap a given collateral type directly for Dai or USDS at a fixed rate, rather than borrowing." Mechanically, "a PSM operates similarly to a regular vault type with a zero Stability Fee and a liquidation ratio of 100% that can only be accessed through a user-facing smart contract containing the relevant swap functions. Unlike regular vaults, users of the PSM do not retain ownership of the asset."

The annotation at A.3.3.2.7.1.1.1.3.0.3.1 draws out what that equivalence means: "Although a PSM has a zero Stability Fee and a liquidation ratio of 100%, it is still a vault and swaps of a collateral asset for Dai represent issuance of Dai that is backed by that collateral asset. The Debt Ceiling serves to limit the exposure the PSM can incur to that collateral asset."

This reframes what looks like a trading venue as a balance-sheet operation. Every PSM swap expands the USDS supply and buys the collateral asset with the newly issued units. The user experiences an exchange; Sky experiences an unlevered, fee-free, permanently open commitment to acquire that asset at par.

Three structural consequences follow. A 100% liquidation ratio means the position can never be liquidated — there is no buffer and no liquidation machinery, so the collateral's value *is* the backing, one-for-one. A zero Stability Fee means Sky earns nothing on the issuance itself, so PSM assets have to earn their keep by being deployed elsewhere. And because the mechanism cannot refuse a swap, the only control on how much of a single asset Sky ends up holding is the debt ceiling — which is why the parameter exists at all, despite there being no credit risk to limit in the usual sense.

The Lite PSM's ceiling machinery (A.3.3.2.7.1.1.1.3–.5) is correspondingly rate-limited rather than fixed: a maximum `line`, a target `gap` between usage and ceiling, and a `ttl` cooldown before the ceiling can rise again — so exposure can grow steadily but cannot jump.
description: PSM swaps look like exchanges but are issuance of Dai or USDS backed by the swapped collateral at a zero stability fee and 100% liquidation ratio, so the ceiling caps single-collateral exposure.
